title: GDExtension definitions lost on refocusing (tabbing back) to Godot project window on macOS
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f, 4.6.3, 4.5.2

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.7) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Whenever I move to another app and then back to the Godot Editor it immediately causes GDExtension definitions to disappear and start showing errors (additionally my full project even crashes when tabbing back), both moving between workspaces and just even in a single workspace just clicking on Firefox in the dock and then back to Godot causes the problem.

Something *might* be wrong with my GDExtension library, but having the engine catch that problem and display a proper error would be better than the current mystery. This problem does not happen on Linux, but whenever I recompile my native library there it *then* causes a crash when next focusing the Godot editor, but I can kind of live with that problem but this problem where *each time* the editor gains focus breaks it on Mac is basically a full blocker on getting anything done so I'm reporting this problem first.

As additional context, on Linux I tried truning off the cmake hot reload option in the GDExtension build for my library, but that didn't seem to change anything.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open a Godot project (using Mobile renderer)
- Make sure the project has a GDExtension library for Mac and there is a GDScript file that uses a constant from the GDExtension library
- Open the script editor and see no errors or even run the game
- Switch to another program (or the running game window)
- Then return to the Godot Editor window and see new errors appear that weren't there. The errors only go away upon restarting Godot

In the example project this is the error that appears:
```
  ERROR: res://scenes/loader.gd:34 - Parse Error: Static function "native_ready()" not found in base "GDScriptNativeClass".
```

And it gets printed everytime the Godot window loses and gains focus.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Here's a project showing the error (I only included the files necessary to trigger the simple case of the error):

[uusi-peliprojekti.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29301462/uusi-peliprojekti.zip)

Opening the loader.gd file in the Godot editor is necessary before being able to trigger the problem.
